record.paper_title: Open Problems on Ultrafilters and Some Connections to the Continuum
record.context_brief: Cardinal invariants from weaker saturation notions
record.original_question: Let p denote the first cardinal κ for which Martin's axiom MA_κ for σ-centered partial orders fails. For weaker saturation notions than the one captured by p, especially those corresponding to combinatorially natural first-order theories such as T_feq, the theory of an existentially closed model of a parametrized family of independent equivalence relations, and T_{3,2}, the theory of the generic tetrahedron-free three-hypergraph, do these weaker notions give rise to natural and interesting cardinal invariants?

There are natural weaker notions corresponding to saturation of some combinatorially natural theories, such as Tfeq ...

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{p}$ denote the pseudo-intersection number, that is, the least cardinal $\kappa$ for which Martin's axiom $\mathrm{MA}_\kappa$ restricted to $\sigma$-centered partial orders fails. (Equivalently, the least cardinality of a family $\mathcal{F}$ of infinite subsets of $\omega$ that is closed under finite intersections, has the strong finite intersection property, and admits no single infinite subset of $\omega$ almost contained in every member of $\mathcal{F}$.)

The invariant $\mathfrak{p}$ may be viewed model-theoretically as a saturation cardinal associated with a particular complete first-order theory. Consider the following two combinatorially natural complete first-order theories:

(a) $T_{\mathrm{feq}}$: the model companion of the theory of a parametrized family of independent equivalence relations. The language has a binary predicate $E(x,y;z)$ such that for each parameter $z$, $E(\cdot,\cdot;z)$ is an equivalence relation, and the family of these equivalence relations is generic/independent; $T_{\mathrm{feq}}$ is the theory of its existentially closed models.

(b) $T_{3,2}$: the theory of the Fraïssé limit (generic structure) of the class of finite $3$-uniform hypergraphs that omit the complete $3$-hypergraph on $4$ vertices (the "tetrahedron-free generic $3$-hypergraph").

For each such theory $T$, one may associate a cardinal invariant $\mathfrak{p}(T)$ measuring the least $\kappa$ for which a natural saturation/realization property at level $\kappa$ fails (analogous to how $\mathfrak{p}$ arises from the saturation of a specific theory), with $\mathfrak{p}(T) \ge \mathfrak{p}$ since these theories are properly weaker (in Keisler's order, or in associated combinatorial complexity) than the theory giving rise to $\mathfrak{p}$.

Problem: Do the weaker saturation notions corresponding to $T_{\mathrm{feq}}$ and $T_{3,2}$ give rise to natural and interesting cardinal invariants of the continuum? In particular, identify such invariants $\mathfrak{p}(T_{\mathrm{feq}})$ and $\mathfrak{p}(T_{3,2})$, determine their ZFC-provable relationships with the standard invariants $\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{t}, \mathfrak{b}, \mathfrak{d}, \dots$, and decide whether any of them can be proved strictly greater than $\mathfrak{p}$ in ZFC.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem asks whether weaker saturation notions, corresponding to theories such as T_feq and T_{3,2}, give rise to natural cardinal invariants. While Malliaris and Shelah's program connects Keisler's order with cardinal invariants of the continuum (most famously proving p = t), the literature available does not record a definitive identification of such invariants for T_feq or T_{3,2}, and the question is posed as an open direction. No source was found announcing a resolution.

status_evidence.title: Cofinality spectrum theorems in model theory, set theory and general topology
status_evidence.snippet: Malliaris–Shelah establish cofinality spectrum theorems relating model-theoretic saturation to cardinal invariants, proving p = t.
status_evidence.claim: The framework connecting saturation of specific theories to cardinal invariants of the continuum is established, but weaker theories like T_feq and T_{3,2} are studied for Keisler-order purposes, not yet yielding identified continuum invariants.

status_evidence.title: Keisler's order has infinitely many classes
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses theories T_{k+1,k} including T_{3,2} producing infinitely many Keisler-order classes via coloring/saturation arguments.
status_evidence.claim: T_{3,2} is shown to occupy a distinct location in Keisler's order, supporting the view that an associated invariant could differ from p, but no continuum invariant is named.
